Unsupervised customer transaction segmentation using K-Means clustering and PCA visualization.

--- ## Overview This repository provides an unsupervised machine learning study on customer financial transactions. It uses K-Means clustering to discover natural behavioral groupings without relying on predefined labels, and applies Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to map high-dimensional transactions into interpretable visual spaces. Downstream supervised models trained on these cluster partitions are documented in [fraud-detection-classification](../fraud-detection-classification). --- ## Clustering Results The optimal number of clusters was evaluated using the Elbow Method and Silhouette Analysis: | Metric | Result | | :--- | :--- | | Optimal Cluster Count (k) | 2 | | Silhouette Score | 0.572 | | Dimensionality Reduction | PCA (2 components) |
### Cluster Visualization (PCA) ![Cluster Visualization](assets/cluster-visualization.png) ### Silhouette Score Analysis ![Silhouette Score](assets/silhouette-score.png)

### Feature Correlation Heatmap ![Correlation Matrix](assets/correlation-matrix.png) ### Feature Distributions ![Feature Distributions](assets/feature-distributions.png) ### Transaction Distribution by Customer Occupation ![Transaction Boxplot](assets/transaction-boxplot.png)
